title: Stonehenge and Great Stones
objective: After this level you can explain what monuments like Stonehenge show about early societies.
summary: Stonehenge took hundreds of workers, stones from Wales and feasts drawing people from across Britain. Göbekli Tepe, about 11,500 years old, was built by hunter-gatherers.

cards.headline: Stonehenge's builders joined giant stones the way a carpenter joins wood.
cards.body: Picture a ring of huge upright stones on a grassy plain, with stone beams laid across their tops. The beams are slotted on with joints you'd normally find in furniture. Monuments like this tell you who built them: how many people, how organized, and what mattered to them.

cards.headline: Built by hundreds, over centuries
cards.body: Stonehenge began as a circular ditch and bank about 3000 BC; the stones went up about 2500 BC. The giant sarsens, about 25 tons each on average, came from about 25 km away. The smaller bluestones came from the Preseli Hills in Wales, more than 200 km away. Moving, shaping and raising them took hundreds of people. That's not a weekend project. That's a society working together.

cards.fact: Some pigs at Stonehenge-era feasts came from as far as north-east Scotland.
cards.context: At Durrington Walls, near Stonehenge, archaeologists have found over 38,000 animal bones. Pig teeth show animals raised in west Wales, northern England and north-east Scotland, then slaughtered at midwinter. Stonehenge itself is lined up with the Sun: at midsummer the sun rises beside the Heel Stone, and at midwinter it set through the tallest arch. People came from far away, at special times of year.

cards.headline: Göbekli Tepe: older than farming
cards.body: In southeastern Turkey, hunter-gatherers began Göbekli Tepe about 11,500 years ago, more than twice Stonehenge's age and before farming. Its T-shaped limestone pillars reach over 5 meters and weigh up to 50 tons. Some are carved with foxes, scorpions and lions. Others have arms and hands carved down their sides, meeting in front over a belt: giant stone people. Building together may have led people to settle, not the other way round.
